answers.explanation: The cache holds copies of what's in use so it can be reached quickly.
Faster storage is checked first. Only on a miss do we go to the slower level.
A hit uses the data straight from the cache.
The OS keeps recently used disk blocks in memory, exactly like a cache.
It's smaller, which is why we need a replacement policy.
Cache size and replacement policy are the two big cache-management decisions.
Because it can't hold everything, you have to choose its size and what to replace.
Deleting files doesn't keep a faster copy of anything.
